findings.F1: Over the idea's own 5-day grid, the bars where the short was active were followed by a coin return 0.74 % below the coin's usual 5-day return (449 cases, t -1.80). The flat bars showed +0.11 % (2970 cases, t 0.53). Five of six coins fell more than usual after active bars, BTC being the exception at +0.11 %. This is the tested idea's own effect, and it is not strong enough to confirm.
findings.F2: The book could not earn from that effect because the coin's drift worked against the short. The normal drift in the short's direction was -0.58 % per 5 days, against an unusual move of +0.45 %, leaving a total move of -0.13 %. That is -0.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip, so the short loses before costs as well as after (book Sharpe -0.22, versus about +0.55 for holding).
findings.F3: None of nine bar conditions sorts the next 5 days' excess return in a graded way. The nine were the 5-day return, the 20-day return, 20-day volatility, distance from the 30-day low, distance from the 30-day high, closing below or above the prior 20-day extremes, the day's range, and relative volume. The mean Spearman per coin was between -0.023 and +0.042, and the quintile means rise and fall without order (for example the 5-day-return quintiles: -0.31 %, -0.45 %, +0.28 %, -0.30 %, +0.38 %).
findings.F4: After larger daily moves the next day tends to reverse, but only weakly. By quintile of the move's size against 20-day volatility, the next day's return signed by the move's direction was -0.10 %, -0.06 %, -0.17 %, -0.25 % (t -2.98) and -0.22 % (t -2.20), on 2900 days each. That is about 0.25 % at best, against a 0.19 % round trip, and from one table among about 57 groups examined.
findings.F5: Next-day returns differ by weekday: +0.42 % after Fridays (t 3.76) and +0.37 % after Thursdays (t 2.63), against -0.12 % after Mondays and -0.18 % after Wednesdays (about 2480 days each). This is a calendar condition with no grade to it, and it is pooled over coins; whether it holds by coin or by year could not be checked because the follow-up exploration failed.

no_ideas: Across the roughly 57 groups examined, chance alone would give a largest |t| near 3. The only patterns at or above that level are an ungraded weekday effect (F5) and a next-day reversal (F4) whose move barely exceeds a round trip's cost, so none stands out enough to support a graded idea.
